title: Expandable routing guardrails for dedicated vs hosted spillover and region/tier fallback
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Redwood currently supports smart routing policies that route inference requests by region, customer tier, and model variant. Two persistent operational patterns have caused customer-visible variability: (1) dedicated capacity exhaustion causing either synchronous failures or opaque fallbacks to hosted variants, and (2) cross-region spillover that increases latency or violates data residency expectations. Existing tickets improved fallback policies and routing matrices, but we lack a compact, extensible set of runtime-level guardrails operators can configure to balance latency SLOs, cost, and compliance.

Problem statement:
- Dedicated pools sometimes overflow into hosted endpoints without clear per-customer controls; this can lead to higher costs and unintended data flow.
- Region selection logic is often reactive and can pick farther regions when nearer capacity is temporarily saturated, harming latency SLOs.
- Fallback model variant selection is not always deterministic; some fallbacks use lower-quality quantized models which may not be acceptable for enterprise customers.
- Operators need predictable, testable policies to ensure application-level SLOs and security/residency constraints are respected during capacity events.

Goals:
1) Introduce a compact "guardrail" policy object that operators (and customer configs) can attach to routing rules to express preferences and hard constraints: prefer_local_region, allow_spillover_to_hosted (enum: never|cost-aware|always), fallback_quality_threshold (e.g., Q0..Q3), max_extra_latency_ms, residency_enforced (boolean).
2) Enforce deterministic routing decision order with observable reason codes for every decision (metrics and traces).
3) Provide a safe default for Hosted Spillover: for customers on Dedicated, default to allow_spillover_to_hosted=cost-aware (only for soft-fallbacks after queued wait and with masking of customer-identifiers), but allow customer override to never.
4) Implement region-aware distance scoring that factors in recent p95 latency to each region and respects residency_enforced.
5) Provide developer-facing simulation CLI and CI check that validates policy changes against synthetic workload traces prior to ship.

Proposed design:
- Policy schema: a JSON-serializable guardrail object stored with the customer's routing config. Key fields: prefer_local_region, spillover_mode, fallback_quality_floor, max_allowed_latency_ms, allowed_regions (whitelist), residency_enforced.
- Decision pipeline changes: Attach policy evaluation layer between capacity scoring and model variant selection. The layer will: (A) filter candidate regions by allowed_regions/residency, (B) score regions by capacity-proximity * latency_history factor * prefer_local_bonus, (C) if no region satisfies max_allowed_latency_ms, apply spillover_mode logic.
- Spillover_mode behavior: "never" -> return capacity_limited error to caller; "cost-aware" -> try to expand to hosted only if model variant quality >= fallback_quality_floor and estimated latency delta <= max_allowed_latency_ms and masking rules satisfied; "always" -> attempt hosted alternatives aggressively but annotate response with fallback_reason.
- Fallback model variant selection: use an ordered list of variants with quality scores (e.g., base, quantized-8, quantized-4). Respect fallback_quality_floor; if no variant meets floor, prefer canary rollbacks or return error.
- Observability: Emit a standardized routing_decision trace with fields as tags: chosen_region, candidate_regions, reason_code (e.g., "SKU_EXHAUSTED","REGION_BLOCKED_BY_POLICY","SPILLOVER_COST_AVOIDED"), fallback_variant, latency_estimate_ms. Expose counter metrics for policy-triggered errors.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- More policy expressivity increases config surface; we provide safe defaults (conservative) and a migration path.
- Enforcing residency adds strictness that may increase errors for some customers but preserves compliance guarantees.
- Cost-aware spillover minimizes surprise billing but requires us to estimate cost deltas; initial approach uses simple heuristics (per-token cost map by model+deployment type).

Acceptance criteria:
- New policy schema documented and accepted in design review.
- Routing decision path updated to consult guardrail layer; unit tests cover key branches.
- Integration tests demonstrate: (A) dedicated pool exhaustion with spillover_mode=never returns capacity error; (B) spillover_mode=cost-aware falls back to hosted only when cost/latency constraints are satisfied; (C) residency_enforced prevents cross-region selection.
- Trace payloads include the routing_decision reason_code and variant chosen.
- Simulation CLI validates 3 synthetic traces and a CI check fails if new policy changes widen p95 latency by >10% in test harness.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind runtime-config for all clusters.
2) Internal alpha: enable for Platform/SE test orgs; collect rollout metrics for 2 weeks.
3) Gradual enable for paying dedicated customers with opt-in.
4) Default-on for new customers after 6 weeks pending validation.

Testing and monitoring:
- Integration scenarios: full-pool exhaustion, transient cold-start spikes, inter-region outage.
- Metrics: per-customer spillover_count, spillover_latency_delta_ms, policy_reject_count, fallback_variant_distribution.
- Alerts: >1% of requests rejected due to spillover_mode=never for dedicated customers (potential capacity/misconfig alert).

Security and compliance notes:
- When spilling to hosted endpoints, sensitive metadata must be redacted unless the customer explicitly allows hosted_spillover_with_cleartext_metadata; default is masked.
- Residency enforcement must integrate with the existing tenancy+VPC annotations.

Docs and artifacts:
- Design doc: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/SmartRouting/ENG-10247-guardrails (placeholder)
- Simulation CLI prototype: git://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-sim/tree/eng-10247
- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4087 (WIP)

Open questions:
- How should we price hosted spillover when cost-aware mode is enabled? Product needs guidance on billing pass-through vs consolidated billing.
- Should we allow variable fallback_quality_floor by route (some routes can accept Q2 while others require Q0)?
- How to surface policy rejections to app owners (HTTP status vs enrich response body) without increasing token plumbing complexity?

Next steps:
- Complete API schema and submit design review by 2026-03-07.
- Implement guardrail layer skeleton and unit tests (ENG) by 2026-03-20.
- Coordinate with Product on billing guidance (PM) and Legal on residency semantics (Security).
